title: Twilight Zone: The Movie
summary: Warner Bros.' theatrical anthology brings the series to cinemas in four segments framed by a late-night drive. Three remake classic episodes, about a retirement home, a boy who reshapes reality and a terrified airline passenger; one new story traps a bigot in the lives of the people he hates. Burgess Meredith narrates. It grossed about $29.45 million in North America on a $10 million budget.
notes: Time Out is an original story by Landis that loosely reworks elements of 'A Quality of Mercy' and 'Back There' (Wikipedia). 'Josh Rogan' is the pseudonym of Melissa Mathison. Jerome Bixby is credited for the short story behind 'It's a Good Life'. Accident note: On July 23, 1982, during filming of the 'Time Out' segment, a helicopter crashed after special-effects explosions, killing Vic Morrow and child actors Myca Dinh Le and Renee Shin-Yi Chen; John Landis was later tried for involuntary manslaughter and acquitted in 1987 (Wikipedia; NTSB report October 1984).

title: Twilight Zone: Rod Serling's Lost Classics
summary: A CBS television film built from material Rod Serling left behind, hosted by James Earl Jones. Richard Matheson expands a Serling outline into "The Theatre," about a moviegoer who sees her own life on the screen, and Serling's own 1968 script "Where the Dead Are" sends a Civil War surgeon to an isolated island where something is wrong. Carol Serling co-produced.
notes: Network: CBS. Executive producers Michael O'Hara and Lawrence Horowitz; producer S. Bryan Hickox; Carol Serling co-producer. IMDb trivia: 'Where the Dead Are' (59 min) is the longest Twilight Zone story.

title: Tower of Terror
summary: A disgraced tabloid reporter and his niece dig into the 1939 disappearance of five guests from a Hollywood hotel elevator on Halloween night, and find the old building is not as empty as it looks. Made for ABC's The Wonderful World of Disney, it was based on the theme-park ride The Twilight Zone Tower of Terror and partly filmed there.
notes: Franchise relation is indirect: the source attraction carries the Twilight Zone name under license, but Wikipedia states the film 'has no connection to any incarnation of The Twilight Zone' (no Serling, no TZ branding). Production companies: Walt Disney Television, Zaloom/Mayfield Productions. Disney's first film based on a park attraction.

title: Rod Serling: Submitted for Your Approval
summary: An American Masters portrait on PBS of Rod Serling, following him from his early live-television dramas through The Twilight Zone and his later struggles with the industry. Lee Grant narrates and Mitch Greenberg voices Serling's own words, while family members and colleagues, among them Mike Wallace, recall the writer.
notes: American Masters (PBS), season 10. Susan Lacy's directorial debut; she was also the series' executive producer (Spokesman-Review, 1995). Change kind from 'film' to 'documentary'; title on site has stray quote marks.

title: The Time Element
summary: Serling's hour-long teleplay for Westinghouse Desilu Playhouse on CBS, widely treated as the series' unofficial pilot. A bartender tells his psychiatrist about a recurring dream in which he wakes up in Honolulu the day before the Pearl Harbor attack and cannot get anyone to heed his warnings. Its success helped persuade CBS to buy The Twilight Zone.
notes: Westinghouse Desilu Playhouse S1 ep 6, CBS; rerun April 6, 1959. Producer Bert Granet bought the script from CBS. Desi Arnaz added an on-stage coda implying it was all a dream. Not officially part of the series.

title: Where Is Everybody? (pilot version)
summary: The sale pilot that became the series premiere of October 2, 1959. A man in an air force jumpsuit wanders a spotless small town with no other people in it. In its first form the narration was spoken by Westbrook Van Voorhis; Serling later re-recorded it himself for broadcast.
notes: Only the Van Voorhis-to-Serling narration change was verified (Wikipedia). Whether a separate unaired cut survives on home video (e.g. Season 1 Blu-ray extras) could not be confirmed; fetch budget ran out. Could be folded into the existing 1959 episode page rather than a separate film record.

title: The Happy Place
summary: Serling's first proposed pilot script for The Twilight Zone, about a society that puts its citizens to death when they reach sixty. CBS executive William Self judged it too bleak to sell to sponsors, and Serling wrote "Where Is Everybody?" as a gentler replacement.

title: The Twilight Zone (Warner Bros. feature in development)
summary: A new Twilight Zone feature that Warner Bros. and Leonardo DiCaprio's Appian Way have tried to develop for more than a decade. Matt Reeves was hired in 2011 and left; Joseph Kosinski entered talks in 2013; a string of writers followed. In June 2025 Ben Stiller was reported to be attached to direct, with the script an open writing assignment.
notes: Timeline per JoBlo (June 10, 2025): Oct 2011 Matt Reeves directing from Jason Rothenberg script; Aug 2013 Kosinski in talks, script by Anthony Peckham; shortly after Aron Eli Coleite (JoBlo spells 'Colette') hired; later drafts Rand Ravich, Joby Harold; 2017 new writer (JoBlo names a 'Christine Lavaf'; name not verified). Producers: Leonardo DiCaprio, Jennifer Davisson. Stiller report originated with Jeff Sneider (The InSneider). Status as of 2026: no confirmed production.

title: The Twilight Zone (stage play)
summary: Anne Washburn's world-premiere stage adaptation weaves several original-series stories by Serling, Beaumont and Matheson into one interlocking evening, staged by Richard Jones. It opened at London's Almeida Theatre and ran to January 27, 2018, then transferred to the West End's Ambassadors Theatre from March 4, 2019.
notes: Episodes adapted not verified from fetched sources (Den of Geek has an article on how stories were selected). Cast listed is the Almeida 2017 company.

title: The Twilight Zone holiday marathons
summary: Syndicated reruns turned the original series into a holiday ritual. WPIX in New York had aired it nightly since the early 1970s, and KTLA in Los Angeles ran an eight-hour marathon on Thanksgiving 1980, then a July 4th marathon from 1983. The New Year's marathon passed to the Sci-Fi Channel, now Syfy, which ran its 22nd annual edition over New Year 2016-17.
notes: Syndication event, not a production. Who ran the first New Year's Eve marathon is unclear (WPIX possibly). 22nd annual Syfy marathon in 2016-17 implies a start around 1994-95 (inference, not stated).
